title: CERT-In Warns of High-Risk Flaws in iPhone, Mac and Other Apple Products
excerpt: India's cybersecurity agency says vulnerabilities across iOS, macOS, Safari, watchOS, tvOS and visionOS could allow code execution and data theft — users should update now.
body:
• CERT-In, India's cybersecurity agency, rated multiple vulnerabilities in Apple products as high risk in an advisory published October 28.
  • Affected software includes iOS and iPadOS before 18.7.11, 26.7.2 or 27.2; macOS Sequoia before 15.8.2, Tahoe before 26.7.2 and Golden Gate before 27.2; Safari before 27.2; and watchOS, tvOS and visionOS before 27.2.
  • Attackers could exploit the flaws through malicious web content, files, images, audio, video or fonts to run code, steal information, bypass controls or crash devices.
  • What to do now: on iPhone or iPad go to Settings > General > Software Update and install the latest version; on Mac use System Settings > General > Software Update.

India's Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) has issued a high-risk advisory warning of multiple vulnerabilities in Apple products, BusinessLine reported on October 28. The agency, which operates under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, said the flaws could let an attacker execute arbitrary code, escalate privileges, disclose sensitive information, bypass security restrictions or cause denial-of-service conditions.

What is vulnerable

The affected list spans nearly the whole Apple ecosystem. According to CERT-In as reported by BusinessLine, it includes Safari versions before 27.2; macOS Sequoia before 15.8.2, macOS Tahoe before 26.7.2 and macOS Golden Gate before 27.2; iOS and iPadOS before 18.7.11, before 26.7.2 and before 27.2; and watchOS, tvOS and visionOS before 27.2. The CSR Journal's account of the same advisory added device context: the iOS branches cover the iPhone XS, XS Max, XR and iPhone 11 and newer, and the iPad branches cover the iPad 7th generation and newer.

https://x.com/TruePatriotVox/status/2115456836614967507

How an attack would work

CERT-In attributed the vulnerabilities to memory corruption, out-of-bounds read and write errors, use-after-free flaws, buffer overflows, race conditions, type confusion, integer overflow, improper input validation and authorization issues across system components including WebKit, the kernel and media-processing frameworks. An attacker could exploit them, the advisory said, by getting a device to process maliciously crafted web content, files, images, audio, video or fonts, or through other vulnerable application interactions — in plain terms, by persuading a user to open or load something hostile.

The target audience, CERT-In warned, is all end-user organizations and individuals using Apple products. That breadth is why the rating matters: this is not a flaw in a single app, but a set of flaws in the operating systems and browser that sit under everyday use.

What users should do

The fix is the update Apple has already released for each platform. As The CSR Journal summarized the guidance: on iPhone and iPad, open Settings, then General, then Software Update; on a Mac, open System Settings, then General, then Software Update; Apple Watch, Apple TV and Vision Pro carry update options in their own settings menus. Users whose older models cannot run the latest major release should still install any security update Apple offers for their supported version.

Not the first warning this year

CERT-In issued a similar high-severity advisory in March this year, warning that vulnerabilities in Apple products could allow remote code execution, system access, security bypass or denial-of-service attacks through iOS and iPadOS versions earlier than 26.4, BusinessLine noted. It issued a similar warning in December 2025 as well. The pattern underlines the practical lesson of this advisory: the risk window is the gap between Apple's patch and the user's update, and closing it is a two-minute settings check.
